name: Silicon Lattice
description: Silicon sp3 tetrahedral geometry at 109.47 degrees. 5D encoding via femtosecond laser: X, Y, Z, birefringence orientation, void size. Theoretical density 10^15 bits/cm3. Phi-spaced shell radii with super-exponential coherence decay.

core_attributes.pattern: tetrahedral sp3 hybridization, 5D femtosecond inscription, φ-shell spacing

scope.definition: Electron drift mobility in high-purity silicon at 300 K as fraction of theoretical phonon-scattering limit — measured by Hall effect in float-zone silicon with dopant density < 10¹²/cm³.

evidence.source: Sze & Ng (2006) 'Physics of Semiconductor Devices', 3rd ed., Wiley; Canali et al. (1975) 'Electron and hole drift velocity measurements in silicon', IEEE Transactions on Electron Devices.
cross_domain_examples: silicon electron mobility 1400 cm²/Vs at 300 K — within 7% of theoretical phonon-limited maximum
gallium arsenide: 8500 cm²/Vs — 6× higher mobility enabling GHz-range transistors
graphene: 200,000 cm²/Vs on hBN substrate — 140× silicon — 2D electron gas removes phonon scattering

scope.falsifiability: If measured silicon Hall mobility consistently exceeds 1600 cm²/Vs at 300 K in multiple independent labs, the phonon scattering limit needs revision.
scope.measurement_limits: Mobility is strongly temperature and dopant-concentration dependent — drops 50% for dopant density >10¹⁵/cm³. Values apply to bulk silicon; thin films show reduced mobility from surface scattering.
